name: Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum
funding: $3.3M expenses (2023); 2025 gifts from individuals, CT Office of the Arts, foundations, Bank of America, Fairfield County Bank, galleries.
watch: Fashion founding fortune. Named funders: Bank of America, Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation (Point72), alcohol (Freixenet Mionetto, Litchfield Distillery). No controversy found.
records_note: Annual reports from 2018 to 2025 are on its site, a named supporters list covers gifts received in 2025, and trustees are listed.

name: Alice Yard
location: Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago
funding: Mellon Foundation USD 150,000 over 36 months (awarded February 2024). Nordic Culture Fund and OCA support residencies; co-rd Ltd and Basso Leonard Architects are listed supporters.
watch: Artist-run space in Belmont, Port of Spain, 20 years old in 2026. Trinbagonians for Palestine supported a 2025 screening.
records_note: The blog's sidebar names two supporters, co-rd Ltd and Basso Leonard Architects, with no date; no reports, accounts or board are published.

name: Almaty Museum of Arts
funding: Opened 12 Sep 2025 for about US$100M (building and collection); Astana Motors (cars, malls) pays running costs, and Halyk Bank has been Lead Partner since Mar 2026.
watch: Private museum of Nurlan Smagulov. Its lead bank partner is majority-owned by Nazarbayev's son-in-law Timur Kulibayev.
records_note: Targeted-use-of-funds reports for 2021 to 2024 are posted; the partners page names only Halyk Bank, undated; the team page lists staff, not a board.

name: Alternative Space LOOP
funding: Non-profit association (2019); 2026 shows supported by Arts Council Korea, supervised by Seoul Metropolitan Government, plus individual LOOP's Friends donors.
watch: Dec 2025 Euljiro move drew a public gentrification inquiry from Cheonggyecheon-Euljiro Preservation Alliance and others.
records_note: Its Support page names its chairs, directors, auditor and 44 individual donors, undated, but it posts no reports or accounts.

name: AlUla Arts & Cultural Oasis
funding: 100% state-funded by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia via the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU), chaired directly by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS).
watch: An authoritarian state mega-project and petro-state artwashing, meant to burnish international prestige amid severe human rights suppression and political imprisonment.

name: A.M. Qattan Foundation
funding: Income GBP 2.6M (2025): Al-Qattan Charitable Trust, Qattan family gifts, Save the Children, Drosos, Taawon, Enabel, Arts Council England, Art Fund.
watch: Barclays (under campaign) is one of its bankers, not a funder. Trust funding paused in 2025 pending a Jersey licence, not as punishment.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2005 to 2025, files audited accounts with the Charity Commission, names donors in its 2025 report, and lists its trustees.

name: Ambasada Kultury
funding: German Federal Foreign Office (PerspAKTIV residencies 2022–2025, run with RAZAM e.V. and Galeria Miejska Arsenał, Poznań, earlier Fundacja IN SITU); CEC ArtsLink residency partnership; no full roster published
watch: Initiative of Belarusian culture workers from Minsk, co-founded by former Ў Gallery directors Valiantsina Kisialeva and Hanna Chystaserdava; projects Open Muzej, Antiwarcoalition.art, EVAa, Secondary Archive. CEC ArtsLink lists it as Berlin-based; its own PerspAKTIV page tags it 'Belarus/Lithuania'.
records_note: A small initiative with no annual report, accounts or board posted; funders such as the Federal Foreign Office appear only in project credits.

name: Amman Design Week
funding: Founded 2016 by Queen Rania; organised with Greater Amman Municipality. 2016 sponsors: Al Manaseer Group, Zain, Aramex, Al Markaziya. 2026: Sukhtian Foundation backs the student exhibition.
watch: 2016 sponsors were Al Manaseer Group, Zain, Aramex and Al Markaziya. The 2026 edition runs 2 to 17 October across Amman and Aqaba.
records_note: ammandesignweek.com returned HTTP 403, so nothing could be checked from its own pages.

name: Amorepacific Museum of Art
funding: Corporate museum run directly by Amorepacific Corp (site footer, 2026); cosmetics money. Current LeWitt show co-organised with MOT Tokyo.
records_note: The museum posts nothing itself; its parent Amorepacific posts audit reports 2015 to 2024, sustainability reports 2017 to 2025 and its board.

name: Aomori Museum of Art
records_note: The museum posts yearly reports from 2006 to 2023 with budget and outturn tables, and an undated list of corporate supporters, but no board list.

name: Apexart
funding: The Andy Warhol Foundation, National Endowment for the Arts, NYSCA, founder endowment; 501(c)(3) non-profit.
watch: Non-profit arts organization in Tribeca, known for its open-call, blind-submission curatorial system.

name: Arab Image Foundation (AIF)
funding: Mellon Foundation, Ford Foundation, AFAC, independent donations; non-profit foundation.
watch: Founded in 1997 by Akram Zaatari, Fouad Elkoury, et al.; holds over 500,000 historic photographs from the Arab world.
records_note: Names its board and funders on its site, undated; its US arm files Form 990s on ProPublica; no annual reports are published.
